summary: A launch failure occurred at NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia when Orbital Sciences Corporation's Antares rocket carrying the Cygnus vehicle with about 5,000 pounds (roughly 2,300 kg) of cargo exploded after liftoff at 6:22 p.m. local time (2222 UTC), creating a massive fireball; nobody was reported injured and the cargo were supplies for the International Space Station, with NASA saying the astronauts will not run out of food or supplies. Orbital vice president Frank Culbertson said the contractor's spacecraft will not fly until the cause of the failure is determined. NASA and Orbital are investigating the explosion, the National Transportation Safety Board is monitoring the investigation, and NASA plans to continue resupplying astronauts once it fully understands what happened; the launch had been delayed a night after a boat entered the hazard area.
